extracted.intended_audience: NOAA public affairs staff, digital media specialists, press officers, and communicators who produce climate/weather press releases
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and required elements for producing NOAA climate- and weather-related press releases, covering scientific, data, communication, and action-oriented requirements and coordination. Intended to ensure accuracy, clarity, and appropriate public-safety and resilience guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be based on best available science
rubrics_metrics.description: News & Features Articles Must: Be based on best available science
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Content should rely on current, validated scientific findings rather than speculation or preliminary, unvetted results. Use peer-reviewed literature or validated datasets where possible and flag preliminary findings as such.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subject matter expert review
rubrics_metrics.description: News & Features Articles Must: Be reviewed by subject matter expert
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Have a qualified SME review technical content for accuracy, interpretive claims, and appropriate caveats before publication. Coordination with program scientists and relevant NOAA line offices (e.g., NWS, NOS) is expected where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: FGDC-compliant metadata for datasets
rubrics_metrics.description: Data Sets Must: Have FGDC-compliant metadata
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Datasets released or referenced in releases must include metadata compliant with Federal Geographic Data Committee standards so users can assess provenance, methods, and limitations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Datasets from validated sources
rubrics_metrics.description: Data Sets Must: Be from validated sources
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use established, vetted data providers and document source validation. Avoid relying on unverified or third-party-processed datasets without clear provenance and quality checks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Datasets include uncertainty estimates
rubrics_metrics.description: Data Sets Must: Include uncertainty estimates
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide numeric or descriptive measures of uncertainty (confidence intervals, error bounds, ensemble spread) for datasets used in the release so readers can assess reliability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish weather from climate
rubrics_metrics.description: Climate vs Weather Distinction: Press releases must clearly differentiate weather (short-term state of the atmosphere) from climate (long-term patterns of weather conditions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly state whether observations or statements describe short-term weather events or longer-term climate trends. This distinction is critical for public understanding and should be reiterated when confusion is likely.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cite peer-reviewed research
rubrics_metrics.description: Scientific Standards: Cite peer-reviewed research
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Link to or reference peer-reviewed literature to support scientific claims. When citing non–peer-reviewed sources, clearly label them and explain limitations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide uncertainty/confidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Implicit Quality: Provide uncertainty/confidence
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quantify and explain uncertainty or confidence in measurements, attributions, and projections. Avoid presenting uncertain results as definitive; use plain-language descriptions of confidence levels where helpful.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use standard climate metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: Scientific Standards: Use standard climate metrics (temperature, sea level, etc.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report observations and trends using established metrics (e.g., mean temperature anomalies, sea-level change) so readers and analysts can compare with other studies and historical baselines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference baseline periods
rubrics_metrics.description: Scientific Standards: Reference baseline periods (e.g., 1991-2020)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When reporting anomalies or trends, state the baseline/reference period used to calculate averages or departures so comparisons are meaningful and transparent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish observed from projected
rubrics_metrics.description: Scientific Standards: Distinguish observed from projected
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clearly label data or statements as observed/historical versus modeled/projection. For projections, provide scenarios or assumptions and associated uncertainty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledge uncertainty in projections
rubrics_metrics.description: Implicit Quality: Acknowledge uncertainty in projections
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When discussing future scenarios, explain the range of possible outcomes and the factors that drive uncertainty; avoid deterministic language for probabilistic projections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plain language
rubrics_metrics.description: Communication Standards: Plain language
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Write for broad audiences using non-technical language. Avoid jargon and complex sentence structures; when technical terms are necessary, define them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Define technical terms
rubrics_metrics.description: Communication Standards: Define technical terms
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide concise definitions for any scientific or technical terms used in the release so non-expert readers can follow the information without ambiguity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish weather events from climate trends
rubrics_metrics.description: Communication Standards / Implicit Quality: Distinguish weather events from climate trends (again emphasized)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When discussing records or extremes, explain whether these are manifestations of underlying climate trends or singular weather events, and avoid conflating the two.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid sensationalism
rubrics_metrics.description: Communication Standards: Avoid sensationalism
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use measured tone and avoid alarmist language. Balance the need to communicate risk with avoiding unnecessary fear; likewise avoid downplaying real risks (see 'avoid both alarmism and false reassurance').

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide context (record-keeping period)
rubrics_metrics.description: Communication Standards: Provide context (record-keeping period)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When reporting records or historical comparisons, state the length of the record (e.g., number of years) and other contextual information that clarifies significance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public safety information when applicable
rubrics_metrics.description: Action-Oriented Elements: Public safety information
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include clear, actionable safety guidance when hazards are involved and coordinate with operational offices (e.g., NWS) to ensure consistency of safety messaging.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resilience and adaptation resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Action-Oriented Elements: Resilience resources and adaptation options
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide links, resources, and practical options communities can use to increase resilience or adapt to impacts when relevant to the release.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide where to get more information
rubrics_metrics.description: Action-Oriented Elements: Where to get more information
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include contacts, links to datasets, further reading, or program pages so audiences and journalists can obtain detailed information or follow up.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multimedia: charts, maps, visualizations
rubrics_metrics.description: Implicit Quality: Multimedia (charts, maps, visualizations)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use visuals to communicate complex information (trends, uncertainty, spatial patterns). Ensure graphics are clear, properly labeled, and accompanied by plain-language captions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coordinate with NWS/NOS/etc as applicable
rubrics_metrics.description: Implicit Quality / Coordination: Coordinated with NWS/NOS/etc as applicable
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure cross-office coordination within NOAA and with partner agencies when releases overlap operational forecasts, navigational impacts, or other mission areas to maintain consistency and accuracy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish trend from variability
rubrics_metrics.description: Special Consideration: Distinguishing trend from variability
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain whether observed changes represent long-term trends or short-term variability and how analysts separate signal from noise. Use statistical or contextual explanations as appropriate for audience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Communicate probabilistic information carefully
rubrics_metrics.description: Special Consideration: Communicating probabilistic information
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Present probabilities and confidence in a way that non-experts can understand (e.g., use frequencies, plain-language descriptors) and avoid presenting single deterministic outcomes when the result is inherently probabilistic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid both alarmism and false reassurance
rubrics_metrics.description: Special Consideration: Avoiding both alarmism and false reassurance
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strike a balanced tone that accurately conveys risks and uncertainties—neither overstating threats nor minimizing them. Use evidence-based framing and SME input to calibrate tone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cultural sensitivity for affected communities
rubrics_metrics.description: Special Consideration: Cultural sensitivity for affected communities
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider the cultural, historical, and socioeconomic context of affected audiences; avoid language or framing that could be insensitive, and provide resources or partners relevant to specific communities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Climate attribution / event attribution guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Special Consideration: Climate attribution science (event attribution)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When attributing events to climate change, rely on appropriate attribution science, clearly state confidence levels, methods, and limitations, and avoid overstating causal claims beyond what evidence supports.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish from individual weather events (explicitly listed)
rubrics_metrics.description: Implicit Quality Item: Distinguish from individual weather events
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make explicit when a press release is not asserting that a single weather event is 'caused by' climate change; if attribution analysis exists, present it with appropriate caveats and methods.
